Conic constraints

Source: R/special-constraints.R
opt_soc_constraint.Rd

Convex cone constraints on affine expressions, solved by conic solvers (Clarabel) and, for second-order cones, by SCIP:

Usage

opt_soc_constraint(model, x, t, name = NULL)

opt_exp_cone(model, x, y, z, name = NULL)

opt_pow_cone(model, x, y, z, alpha, name = NULL)

opt_psd_constraint(model, M, name = NULL)

Arguments

model

An opt_model().

x, y, z, t

Affine expressions; x in opt_soc_constraint() may be a vector, all others are scalars.

name

Optional name.

alpha

Exponent of the power cone.

M

Square affine matrix expression.

Value

An opt_special_constraint reference, invisibly.

Details

  • opt_soc_constraint(): \(\|x\|_2 \le t\) (second-order cone).

  • opt_exp_cone(): \(y \exp(x / y) \le z\) with \(y > 0\) (the closure of the exponential cone, as in Clarabel and SCS).

  • opt_pow_cone(): \(x^\alpha y^{1-\alpha} \ge |z|\) with \(x, y \ge 0\) and \(0 < \alpha < 1\).

  • opt_psd_constraint(): the symmetric matrix M is positive semidefinite. Only the upper triangle of M is used, so symmetry must hold by construction (for example with opt_sym_variable()).

All arguments must be affine in the decision variables after parameter substitution. Models with cones are classified as "SOCP" (second-order cones only) or "CONIC", with "MI" prefixed when integer variables are present; they are convex when the objective is linear or a convex quadratic and all rows are linear.

Examples

# distance from the origin to the line x + y = 2
m <- opt_model()
x <- opt_variable(m, "x", dim = 2)
t <- opt_variable(m, "t")
opt_constraint(m, sum(x) == 2)
opt_soc_constraint(m, x, t)
opt_objective(m, t)
opt_objective_value(opt_solve(m))  # sqrt(2)
#> [1] 1.414214
